info.title: Portitor management API
info.description: Reads a provider's catalog, starts and follows contract negotiations and transfers in which this connector is the consumer, reads and ends the transfers it runs as provider, and shows the dataset harvest jobs (read only). Served on its own port (PORTITOR_MANAGEMENT_BIND), never on the DSP port. Every call except this description, the health checks (/api/check/...) and GET /health needs the API key. Without PORTITOR_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY_FILE, the port serves the health checks only. The API key is opaque (see the api_key security scheme). HTTP 403 is reserved for tokens with limited rights in 1.x; 1.0 never answers it. Every route answers 503 with a problem document when the request took longer than 60 seconds; at most 4 catalog or dataset answers are read from providers at a time, and a further request waits within those 60 seconds. The data plane token (the authorization property of a transfer's dataAddress) is opaque too: send it as it is, do not parse it; a 1.x release may issue another form.

post.summary:
Read one dataset from a provider (DSP 2025-1 `Dataset`), by its
`@id`. Works as `POST /v1/catalog/request` does: the connector's own
DCP token, one try, the provider's JSON as it came.

200.description: The dataset (DSP 2025-1 Dataset), as the provider sent it

400.description: Invalid request, a protocol other than dataspace-protocol-http:2025-1, a dataset id that is "." or "..", or an address that is not an https URL

403.description: Reserved for scoped access in 1.x (ADR 0025): the caller is known but may not make this call. Not returned today. The API key (PORTITOR_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY_FILE) keeps every right and never gets this answer.

502.description: No dataset: the provider refused (the detail has its HTTP status; 404 for a dataset it does not have or does not show us), did not answer, answered with something that is not a JSON object or whose @type is not Dataset (a dataset without @type is accepted), or the identity component gave no token

post.summary:
Read a provider's catalog (DSP 2025-1 `Catalog`): the datasets it
offers, each with its offers (`hasPolicy`). The connector asks the
provider with its own DCP token and waits for the answer (one try, at
most 30 seconds); nothing is stored.
post.description:
The answer is the provider's JSON as it came. At most 16 MiB are
read. The catalog's `participantId` must be the `counterPartyId` of
the request: the catalog of another participant, or one without a
`participantId` (DSP 2025-1 requires it), is answered with 502 and
not handed on. No setting turns this check off. The two ids are
compared as written, with one exception: in a `did:web` DID the
escaped colon before a port may be `%3A` or `%3a`. If the provider sends its catalog in pages (DSP 2025-1, "Catalog
HTTPS Binding", "Pagination"), this is the first page only, and the
provider's `Link` headers are copied to the answer.

200.description: The provider's catalog (DSP 2025-1 Catalog), as the provider sent it

Link.description: The provider's Link headers, when it sent its catalog in pages; only this first page is returned

400.description: Invalid request, a protocol other than dataspace-protocol-http:2025-1, a querySpec, or an address that is not an https URL

403.description: Reserved for scoped access in 1.x (ADR 0025): the caller is known but may not make this call. Not returned today. The API key (PORTITOR_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY_FILE) keeps every right and never gets this answer.

502.description: No catalog: the provider refused (the detail has its HTTP status), did not answer, answered with more than 16 MiB or with something that is not a Catalog, answered with a Catalog whose participantId is not the counterPartyId of the request (or that has none), or the identity component gave no token

post.summary:
End a transfer this connector runs as provider. Access ends at once:
the data flow is terminated and every download of it that runs is
cut. The DSP termination is sent to the consumer in the background;
the state becomes `TERMINATED` once the consumer acknowledges it, or
when it cannot be reached. Asked again while the termination is on
its way, it answers the same and sends nothing more.

202.description: Access ended; termination on its way

403.description: Reserved for scoped access in 1.x (ADR 0025): the caller is known but may not make this call. Not returned today. The API key (PORTITOR_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY_FILE) keeps every right and never gets this answer.

post.summary:
Request a transfer as consumer, under an agreement from one of our
negotiations. The request is sent in the background; follow the
transfer with `GET /v1/transfers/{consumerPid}` until it is `STARTED`
and has a `dataAddress` (pull), or until it has an `objectKey` (push).
A push transfer is completed by the provider once the data is in the
push bucket.

400.description: Invalid request, no finalized negotiation holds the agreement, or HttpData-PUSH without object storage and a push bucket

403.description: Reserved for scoped access in 1.x (ADR 0025): the caller is known but may not make this call. Not returned today. The API key (PORTITOR_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY_FILE) keeps every right and never gets this answer.

get.summary: One transfer, with its data address once the provider started it.

post.summary:
Complete a `STARTED` transfer: we have the data and need no more. The
completion is sent in the background.

202.description: Completion on its way; the state changes once the provider acknowledges it

400.description: The transfer is not STARTED, or a message is still on its way

403.description: Reserved for scoped access in 1.x (ADR 0025): the caller is known but may not make this call. Not returned today. The API key (PORTITOR_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY_FILE) keeps every right and never gets this answer.

post.summary:
Start a `SUSPENDED` transfer again, whichever party suspended it (DSP
2025-1 lets either party start it again). The token in `dataAddress`
stays the same and works again once the transfer is `STARTED`; the
provider sends no new address (ADR 0013). The start message is sent in
the background (added in 1.1).

202.description: Start message on its way; the state changes once the provider acknowledges it

400.description: The transfer is not SUSPENDED, or a message is still on its way

403.description: Reserved for scoped access in 1.x (ADR 0025): the caller is known but may not make this call. Not returned today. The API key (PORTITOR_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY_FILE) keeps every right and never gets this answer.

post.summary:
Suspend a `STARTED` transfer: the provider's data plane refuses the
token until the transfer is started again. The suspension is sent in
the background (added in 1.1).

202.description: Suspension on its way; the state changes once the provider acknowledges it

400.description: The transfer is not STARTED, or a message is still on its way

403.description: Reserved for scoped access in 1.x (ADR 0025): the caller is known but may not make this call. Not returned today. The API key (PORTITOR_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY_FILE) keeps every right and never gets this answer.

post.summary:
End a transfer that has not ended yet. The termination is sent in the
background.

202.description: Termination on its way; the state changes once the provider acknowledges it

400.description: The transfer has ended, or a message is still on its way

403.description: Reserved for scoped access in 1.x (ADR 0025): the caller is known but may not make this call. Not returned today. The API key (PORTITOR_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY_FILE) keeps every right and never gets this answer.

CatalogRequest.description:
Ask a provider for its catalog.

The body is the `CatalogRequest` of Eclipse EDC's management API v4
(EDC v1.0.0-RC8: `catalog-request-schema.json` in
`management-api-schema-validator`, `CatalogRequest.java` and
`CatalogRequestValidator.java`), so a client written for EDC can send
the same body. What Portitor does with each member:

- `counterPartyAddress`, `counterPartyId`: required, as in EDC. A
  negotiation (`POST /v1/negotiations`) names the provider with the same
  two members.
- `protocol` or `profile` (EDC's newer name for it): exactly one is
  required, as in EDC's schema, and it must be
  `dataspace-protocol-http:2025-1`, the only protocol this
  connector speaks. Any other value is refused with 400.
- `additionalScopes`: optional, honoured as in EDC: the scopes are
  added to the configured ones in the token for the provider.
- `querySpec`: refused with 400 when present. EDC sends it to the
  provider as the `filter` of the `CatalogRequestMessage`; DSP 2025-1
  leaves the content of `filter` to each implementation, and a
  provider that does not support it must refuse the request, as
  Portitor's own provider side does. Portitor always asks for the
  whole catalog.
- `@context`: optional and not read. EDC requires it (its bodies are
  JSON-LD); Portitor reads the member names as written.
- `@type`: optional; when present it must be `CatalogRequest`.
- Any other member (EDC's schema also lists `@id`, which EDC does
  not use) is refused with 400, as on every management call.

@context.description:
Accepted so that a body written for Eclipse EDC works unchanged;
not read.

additionalScopes.description:
Scopes the provider may read from our Credential Service with our
token, on top of the configured ones (`PORTITOR_DCP_SCOPES`): for
datasets a provider shows only to holders of a credential.

counterPartyAddress.description:
The provider's DSP endpoint, for example
`https://provider.example/dsp/2025-1`: the `counterPartyAddress`
of a negotiation. The catalog is read at
`<counterPartyAddress>/catalog/request`.

counterPartyId.description:
The provider's participant id: a `did:web` DID, the
`counterPartyId` of a negotiation. Our token is made for it, and
the catalog must name it as its `participantId`.

profile.description: Eclipse EDC's newer name for `protocol`; the same value.

protocol.description:
`dataspace-protocol-http:2025-1`. Exactly one of `protocol` and
`profile` is required.

querySpec.description:
Not supported: a request with a `querySpec` is refused with 400.
The whole catalog is always asked for.

ComponentResult.description: The result of one check: EDC's `HealthCheckResult`.

oneOf.description: Why it failed; `null` when it passed (always present).

DatasetRequest.description:
Ask a provider for one dataset.

The body is the `DatasetRequest` of Eclipse EDC's management API v4
(EDC v1.0.0-RC8: `dataset-request-schema.json`, `DatasetRequest.java`
and `DatasetRequestValidator.java`). `@id` (the dataset's id),
`counterPartyAddress` and `counterPartyId` are required, and exactly
one of `protocol` and `profile`; all are read as in
[`CatalogRequest`]. EDC's `DatasetRequest` has no `querySpec` and no
`additionalScopes`, so neither is taken here.

@context.description:
Accepted so that a body written for Eclipse EDC works unchanged;
not read.

@id.description: The dataset's `@id` in the provider's catalog.

counterPartyAddress.description:
The provider's DSP endpoint. The dataset is read at
`<counterPartyAddress>/catalog/datasets/<@id>`.

counterPartyId.description: The provider's participant id: a `did:web` DID.

profile.description: Eclipse EDC's newer name for `protocol`; the same value.

protocol.description:
`dataspace-protocol-http:2025-1`. Exactly one of `protocol` and
`profile` is required.

failureDetail.description: The messages joined with `", "`, as EDC's `getFailureDetail()`.

messages.description: What went wrong. Never a secret, key or token.

HarvestCountsView.description: What a harvest run did, counted.

added.description: Datasets that entered the catalog (new, or back after a withdrawal).

rejected.description: Entries that failed a check; the previous version, if any, stays.

seen.description: Entries in the snapshot (or stored datasets checked again).

unchanged.description: Datasets that passed with the same content.

updated.description: Datasets whose content or state changed.

withdrawn.description:
Datasets no longer in the source: out of the catalog, kept for
transfers under agreements already made.

datasetId.description: The dataset's `@id`, if it could be read.

position.description:
The entry's position in the source, from 0; absent for a stored
dataset checked again (`bundle` job).

report.description:
The report of the check, for example a SHACL validation report. A
SHACL report keeps its first 50 results; `resultsNotStored` says
how many more there were.

errors.description:
The entries it rejected, in the order it found them: at most the
first 1000 (`counts.rejected` has the total, and the summary says
when some were not stored).

HarvestJobDetail.description: A harvest job with its entry errors.

next.description: Pass as `after` to get the next (older) page; absent on the last page.

HarvestJobView.description: A harvest run: of the datasets, or of the authority's bundle.

id.description: The job id; a newer job has a higher id.

kind.description:
What it harvested: `datasets`, or `bundle` (a check for a new
version of the authority's schema and vocabulary bundle; its
counts are all 0, and its summary says which version is in use).

outcome.description:
`succeeded` (nothing rejected; for a bundle, a new version is in
use), `partial` (some entries rejected), `unchanged` (same snapshot
as the last run; for a bundle, no newer version) or `failed` (the
source could not be read, or a new bundle version was refused; the
catalog and the rules were left as they were).

snapshotSha256.description:
SHA-256 of the snapshot (for a bundle, of the new version's
`manifest.json`), hex; absent when the source failed, nothing new
was fetched, or the stored datasets were checked again.

source.description:
The source's name, for example `file:/etc/portitor/datasets.json`,
or the bundles' URL.

summary.example: 3 seen, 1 added, 0 updated, 2 unchanged, 0 withdrawn, 0 rejected

trigger.description:
What started it: `start`, `interval`, or `bundle` (a new bundle
version came in, so the stored datasets were checked again).

HealthStatus.description: The answer of every check route: EDC's `HealthStatus`.

isSystemHealthy.description:
Whether every component is healthy. False when there is no
component at all, as in EDC.

negotiations.description: The negotiations, in consumer pid order.

next.description: Pass as `after` to get the next page; absent on the last page.

NegotiationView.description: A negotiation this connector runs as consumer.

agreement.description:
The agreement (DSP 2025-1 `Agreement`), once the provider sent it.
Valid for use once `state` is `FINALIZED`.

counterPartyAddress.description:
The other party's DSP endpoint: the provider's, as this connector
is the consumer of every negotiation it lists.

counterPartyId.description: The other party's participant id: the provider's.

providerPid.description: The provider's process id, once it has answered.

state.description: The DSP state, for example `REQUESTED` or `FINALIZED`.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 problem details.

detail.description: What went wrong in this case.

title.description: Short summary of the problem type.

ProvidedTransferPage.description: One page of transfers as provider.

next.description: Pass as `after` to get the next page; absent on the last page.

transfers.description: The transfers, in provider pid order.

ProvidedTransferView.description: A transfer this connector runs as provider.

agreementId.description: The agreement the transfer is made under.

counterPartyAddress.description: Where our messages to the consumer go (its `callbackAddress`).

counterPartyId.description: The consumer's participant id (its DID), proven by its DCP token.

datasetId.description: The dataset whose data is transferred.

format.description: The format the consumer asked for.

messageOnItsWay.description:
Whether a message of ours is on its way to the consumer (for
example the termination, until the consumer acknowledges it).

providerPid.description: Our process id; also the id of its data flow (`/data/{providerPid}`).

state.description: The DSP state, for example `REQUESTED` or `STARTED`.

StartNegotiation.description:
Start a negotiation as consumer.

The other party is named as in the catalog calls and as Eclipse EDC
names it: `counterPartyAddress` and `counterPartyId` (before 0.13:
`providerAddress` and `providerId`, which are now refused as unknown
members). EDC's `ContractRequest` and `TransferRequest` carry only
`counterPartyAddress` (EDC v1.0.0-RC8, `ContractRequest.java`,
`TransferRequest.java`); `counterPartyId` is the name of EDC's
`CatalogRequest` and of its `ContractNegotiation` view, and Portitor
requires it here, because its token is made for that participant.

counterPartyAddress.description:
The provider's DSP endpoint, for example
`https://provider.example/dsp/2025-1` (the catalog's
`DataService` `endpointURL`).

counterPartyId.description:
The provider's participant id (the catalog's `participantId`): a
`did:web` DID. Our DSP requests are tokens for it, and only it may
answer.

datasetId.description:
The dataset id. Optional if the offer has a `target`; offers in a
catalog have none, as the dataset holds them. An empty one is
refused.

offer.description:
The offer from the provider's catalog (a DSP 2025-1 `Offer`), copied
unchanged from the dataset's `hasPolicy`.

agreementId.description:
The `@id` of the agreement of one of our `FINALIZED` negotiations.
The transfer is requested from the provider of that negotiation.

format.description:
A format of one of the dataset's distributions: `HttpData-PULL`
(the default), or, since 1.1, `HttpData-PUSH`, where the provider
sends the data to this connector, which stores it in its push
bucket. `HttpData-PUSH` needs the object storage settings and
`PORTITOR_PUSH_BUCKET`; without them the request is refused (400).

next.description: Pass as `after` to get the next page; absent on the last page.

transfers.description: The transfers, in consumer pid order.

TransferView.description: A transfer this connector runs as consumer.

agreementId.description: The agreement the transfer is made under.

counterPartyAddress.description:
The other party's DSP endpoint: the provider's, as this connector
is the consumer of every transfer it lists.

counterPartyId.description: The other party's participant id: the provider's.

dataAddress.description:
Where to fetch the data, with the access token (DSP 2025-1
`DataAddress`): send `GET <endpoint>` with `Authorization: Bearer
<the authorization property>` (its `authType` property says
`bearer`). Present while the transfer is `STARTED` or `SUSPENDED`;
the token works only while it is `STARTED`. The token is an opaque
string: send it as it is and do not parse it; a 1.x release may
issue another form.

objectKey.description:
A push transfer (`HttpData-PUSH`, since 1.1): the key of the object
in the push bucket (`PORTITOR_PUSH_BUCKET`) that holds the data,
once data has arrived. A push transfer never has a `dataAddress`.

providerPid.description: The provider's process id, once it has answered.

state.description: The DSP state, for example `REQUESTED` or `STARTED`.

api_key.description: The key from PORTITOR_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY_FILE: Authorization: Bearer <key>. The key is an opaque string: a client must not parse it or rely on its length or alphabet, and a 1.x release may accept other forms of token.

tags.name: Catalog
tags.description: A provider's catalog and datasets, read as consumer (DSP 2025-1). The request bodies are those of Eclipse EDC's management API v4.

tags.name: Transfers
tags.description: Transfer processes as consumer (DSP 2025-1), pull only

tags.name: Provided transfers
tags.description: Transfer processes as provider (DSP 2025-1): read them, and end one, which ends access at once (ADR 0027)

tags.name: Harvest
tags.description: Dataset harvest runs: datasets come from the source into the catalog (ADR 0020). Read only.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Health checks in Eclipse EDC's Observability API shape (ADR 0023). They need no API key, and neither does GET /health (plain `ok`). Served even when the management API is off.
